newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian charged with massacre heads back to court.
newsitem.headline: Australian charged with massacre heads back to court.

text.p: The man accused of killing 35 people in Australia's worst mass murder in recent history will make an unexpected court appearance next week, defence and prosecution lawyers said on Wednesday.

Martin Bryant, 29, who pleaded not guilty in September to the killings in the southern island state of Tasmania in April, will attend pre-trial discussions on Thursday in the Supreme Court in the state capital, Hobart, they said.

Bryant's trial is due to begin under heavy security on November 19. He has so far only appeared once in court since his arrest on April 29, the morning after a gunman opened fire on visitors at a popular tourist spot in the island's southeast.
On September 30, he pleaded not guilty to a total of 72 charges, including counts of attempted murder, grievous bodily harm, assault and arson.

"It's appropriate that these (pre-trial) discussions, which will involve the trial process, should take place in the presence of Martin Bryant," defence lawyer John Avery and chief prosecutor Damian Bugg said in a joint statement.
"It is expected that he will appear. No other indication can and will be given as to the nature of these discussions."
